findings: Amsterdam applies additional municipal rules alongside national rental law.
Social and regulated mid-market rental housing is subject to additional allocation/occupancy requirements, including a housing permit for the tenant where applicable.
Rental is not permitted where the dwelling is still subject to purchase protection unless an applicable permit or exemption exists.
Purchase protection applies through the Huisvestingsverordening and generally prevents qualifying newly purchased dwellings from being rented for four years without a permit or exemption.

The current 2026 regulation contains multiple value categories and conditions; the decisive value and scope must be determined from the current regulation and acquisition circumstances rather than an older public-information threshold.
The protection is linked to acquisition after the introduction of the regime and contains conditions concerning prior rental/use.

Permit grounds include rental to first- or second-degree relatives and temporary rental for at most one year after the owner has occupied the dwelling for at least one year; other statutory/regulatory grounds and exemptions also exist.
Application evidence includes the deed of transfer, applicable WOZ information and situation-dependent supporting documents.
A municipal room-rental permit is required where the Amsterdam room-rental regime applies.
General conditions include a communal room of at least 11 m2 and at least 3 metres wide, occupancy limits per room, individual rental contracts and fire-safety compliance.
For four or more rooms additional acoustic requirements apply; for five or more rooms a fire-safety notification through the Omgevingsloket is required.
A dwelling still subject to purchase protection cannot use the ordinary room-rental route unless the purchase-protection requirements are separately satisfied.
Where the applicable spatial plan permits only one household, an additional environmental/planning permit may be required.
The number of permits possible in a building is assessment-dependent and therefore cannot be determined from a simple citywide yes/no rule.
Holiday rental requires registration/permit and advance notification under Amsterdam's tourist-rental regime.
The general annual maximum is 30 nights and no more than four guests at a time.

From 1 April 2026 the annual maximum is 15 nights in specified neighbourhoods in Centrum and De Pijp: Haarlemmerbuurt, Jordaan, Grachtengordel-West, Grachtengordel-Zuid, De Weteringschans, Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde, Nieuwmarkt/Lastage and Oude Pijp.
The 15-night rule is explicitly geographic, so address/neighbourhood resolution is mandatory.
Bed & breakfast, holiday rental and short stay are separate legal categories and must not be merged into one rule.
Short stay is separately permit-regulated under the Huisvestingsverordening.
The Huisvestingsverordening treats short stay as a distinct form of tourist rental and prohibits use of a dwelling for short stay without a municipal permit.
The housing-regulation definition is its own legal framework and should not be assumed identical to spatial-plan definitions.

Amsterdam also uses a contractual/policy self-occupancy rental prohibition for qualifying new-build owner-occupied homes; this is legally distinct from statutory purchase protection for existing housing.
Published exceptions include first-degree family rental, temporary foreign stay, rental within the regulated mid-market price limit and exceptional hardship cases.

decisionModelRequirements: Resolve exact address/BAG location before evaluating area-dependent rules.
Determine acquisition date, prior rental/use and applicable WOZ value before evaluating purchase protection.
Determine rental type: whole dwelling, room rental, holiday rental, B&B, short stay or temporary rental.
Check current Huisvestingsverordening version and current Nadere regels at query time.
Check applicable omgevingsplan where room rental, dwelling formation/splitting or one-household restrictions may apply.
Apply neighbourhood override for the 15-night tourist-rental areas from 1 April 2026.
Keep new-build contractual self-occupancy restrictions separate from statutory purchase protection.
